observations: Single photo shows a blue cast-metal gear reducer (gearbox) sitting on bare ground, output shaft visible on the right side.
A metal nameplate is visible on top of the housing but the text on it is too small/blurred to read.
No separate electric motor is visible anywhere in the frame; only the gearbox unit is shown.
A watermark reading 'CHIDONBEST INDUSTRIAL' overlays the image; this is the seller/reseller's branding, not a product brand.
Surface shows normal paint wear and some dirt/oxidation consistent with used industrial equipment, but no close-up of seals, shaft coupling, or oil ports.

claims.claim: Industrial gear box and electric motor 20hp
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows only the gearbox; no motor of any size is visible in the frame.
Nameplate on photo 0 is present but text is unreadable, so the ratio cannot be confirmed from the image.

risks.risk: No motor is pictured despite being part of the listing, so its existence, horsepower, and condition cannot be confirmed.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the electric motor itself, showing its nameplate with HP, voltage, and RPM.
risks.if_unproven: priced as gearbox only, with no motor included

risks.risk: Gearbox brand, model, and true reduction ratio are unknown since the nameplate is illegible.
risks.proof: A close-up, in-focus photo of the gearbox nameplate.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic unbranded industrial gearbox of unknown ratio

risks.risk: Internal condition (gear wear, bearing play, oil leaks) cannot be assessed from an exterior static photo on dirt ground.
risks.proof: A video of the shaft being rotated by hand showing smoothness and no excessive play, plus a photo of the oil level/seal area.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not confirmed working, worst case needing overhaul

risks.risk: Item is shown sitting directly on bare soil, suggesting long outdoor storage which can mean rust or water ingress inside housing.
risks.proof: Photos of the storage location and close-ups of seals/flanges for rust staining.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the gearbox nameplate (brand, model, ratio, serial).
Photo(s) of the actual electric motor with its nameplate showing HP, voltage, RPM.
Video of the gearbox shaft being turned by hand to check for smoothness/play.
Photo of oil seals and flange areas for rust or leakage.
response.reason: The gearbox's nameplate, which sets its model and ratio, is unreadable, and the claimed 20hp motor is entirely absent from the photo, so no worst-case price can be anchored without further proof of these two core items.
